purpose: Teach: キッカケ/曇っ/わるい/じつに/ていねい/いまどき/ことさら/べつに

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとの出会いがキッカケで仕事を始めたぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father and I first met — that's what got me into this line of work.
lines.style: Slow, measured recall. Voice softens on the memory. Slight pause before 'that's what got me.' Steady gaze, looking inward. The weight of time in every phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、空が曇った日には書道をなさったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mmm, yes — and you'd always do your calligraphy on those cloudy days, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle interjection, like she's been holding this detail for decades. Warm, slightly playful. A small smile in the voice. The 'didn't you' is tender confirmation, not a question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはわるい話には乗らない方だったぞ
lines.en: Gran, your father — he never got caught up in anything unseemly back then.
lines.style: Measured, almost ceremonial. Speaking of principle as if it still matters. Quiet pride underneath. Slight emphasis on 'never' — a small defense of a memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、じつに勤勉でいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, and he was such a diligent man in those days, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Nostalgic agreement, overlapping his thought with her own memory. Soft, knowing tone. The 'wasn't he' carries both admiration and gentle teasing — she knew him in ways he's only remembering now.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんはていねいに毎日の日記を付けていらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, he kept a diary every single day — so careful with it, so faithful.
lines.style: Voice lightens slightly, finding something almost gentle in the routine. The words come slowly, as if seeing the ink dry on each page. No rush. This matters.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、いまどきのお話にも興味をお持ちだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he was always so interested in what people were doing, in the world around him, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Animated but not loud. A woman who remembers being surprised by his curiosity. Warm, almost protective of this detail. The 'wasn't he' carries genuine question — she's inviting him to agree with her version.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはお孫様にことさら優しかったぞ
lines.en: Your father — he had such a soft place in his heart for the grandchildren back then.
lines.style: Voice catches slightly on 'soft place.' The words come slower. This is tender ground. Breath beneath the words, not above them. Speaking of something that still means everything.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、不平はべつに仰らない方だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He never complained, you know — not really. That wasn't his way, was it, dear?
lines.style: Close, intimate whisper. Like she's telling him a secret he already knows. The voice is small but steady. A lifetime of not hearing him complain, and she's guarding that memory like it was precious. Soft fadeout at the end.
